newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore divorce rate up 14.6 percent to 4,110.
newsitem.headline: Singapore divorce rate up 14.6 percent to 4,110.

text.p: The number of divorces in Singapore climbed 14.64 percent to 4,110 in 1995 from 3,585 the previous year, the government's Statistics Department said in a report on Wednesday.
Two-thirds of all divorce petitions were instituted by the wife, the report said.
The divorce rate was higher among younger Singaporeans with the rate for those aged 20-24 years at 15 per 1,000 for men and 16 per 1,000 for women, the Statistics Department said.
The main reason for divorce among non-Moslem couples, meaning mainly ethnic Chinese, was that the marriage partners had lived apart or were separated for three years or more.
The next leading cause of divorce was unreasonable behaviour. Adultery was cited by only 4.6 percent of petitioners for divorce.
Ethnic Chinese make up at least 70 percent of Singapore's three million population.
Among Moslems, mainly Malay people, personality differences and neglect were cited by 64 percent of those seeking divorce.
